channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Haddad chama Flávio de “bolsonarinho” e de protetor de super-ricos
item.description: Former Finance Minister Fernando Haddad (PT-SP) used X to attack Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), calling him "bolsonarinho" and accusing him of spreading misinformation about the tax reform. Haddad clarifies that the reform does not increase taxes for entrepreneurs who already paid income tax at source, but targets those earning over R$1 million annually, and criticizes Bolsonaro’s government for freezing the tax table during the pandemic, harming low-income earners.

item.title: Malabarismos verbais
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema criticized the Supreme Court after Justice Gilmar Mendes requested his inclusion in the fake news investigation over a puppet satire. Zema said Mendes is turning an internet joke about Alexandre de Moraes threatening critics into reality. The full article is available only to subscribers.

item.title: 'Família Bolsonaro não deve se meter mais nas eleições do Rio, porque só apresentam ladrão', diz deputado ex-bolsonarista Otoni de Paula
item.description: Federal deputy Otoni de Paula (PSD-RJ), a former Bolsonaro supporter, strongly criticizes the Bolsonaro family for their backing of Rio de Janeiro governors, accusing them of causing the state's crisis, which he describes as a 'narco-state'. He claims the Bolsonaro family 'only presents thieves' and should no longer interfere in Rio's elections, advocating support for Eduardo Paes (PSD) as an alternative.

item.title: Sem pedido formal do DF, governo Lula mantém distância de plano para salvar BRB
item.description: The federal government of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has not received any formal request from the Distrito Federal to intervene or authorize the credit operation aimed at rescuing the Bank of Brasília (BRB), which is involved in billion-dollar frauds with Banco Master. Governor Celina Leão’s (PP) administration is negotiating with the Credit Guarantee Fund (FGC) and private banks to structure the bailout, but without official federal involvement so far. The article highlights the lack of institutional dialogue between federal and district governments regarding the BRB crisis.

item.title: Fraude no INSS: um ano após operação revelar desvios, ressarcimento a segurados chega a quase R$ 3 bilhões
item.description: One year after Operation Sem Desconto exposed irregular deductions from INSS pensions and retirement benefits, the agency has refunded R$ 2.95 billion to 4.34 million beneficiaries, with total fraud estimated at up to R$ 6.3 billion between 2019 and 2024. President Lula signed a law banning associational deductions from INSS benefits but vetoed the provision requiring active beneficiary outreach and automatic reimbursement, citing legal risks, operational burdens, and extraordinary costs without a budgetary impact assessment. The deadline to contest improper deductions has been extended to June 20, with approximately 4 million beneficiaries yet to respond.

item.title: Procurador da Alerj vai a Brasília tentar destravar sucessão no governo do Rio
item.description: The Alerj prosecutor, Pedro Ricardo Ferreira Queiroz, traveled to Brasília to seek a direct dialogue with STF Minister Cristiano Zanin to resolve the impasse over the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial succession. Following the conviction of former governor Cláudio Castro and Zanin’s injunction keeping TJ-RJ President Ricardo Couto in interim command of the Guanabara Palace, the Alerj now argues that its newly elected president, Douglas Ruas (PL), has a legal right to assume the governorship. However, the STF maintains the injunction remains in force until the case is fully judged, and Ruas’s effort is seen as having low chances of success, with the main goal being to formally notify the Court of the new successor.

item.title: Fla estreia na Copa do Brasil com triunfo de 2 a 1 sobre o Vitória
item.description: Flamengo debuted in the 2026 Copa do Brasil with a 2-1 victory over Vitória. Although the match started evenly, the technical superiority of the team led by Portuguese coach Leonardo Jardim made the difference in the final stage, six minutes into the second half, securing the win.

item.title: Portugal diz a Lula que imigração é digna, mas brasileiros expõem outra realidade
item.description: President Lula's visit to Portugal highlighted a gap between the Portuguese government's official discourse that immigration is dignified and the reality faced by Brazilians seeking citizenship or regularization, who often encounter bureaucracy and practical obstacles.

item.title: Após ganhar vitrine em embate com STF, Zema vira alvo de bolsonaristas
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo), a pre-candidate for presidency, gained media visibility by confronting the STF, especially after being included in the fake news inquiry by Minister Gilmar Mendes. This exposure, however, has caused discomfort among hardline Bolsonarists who support Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) as the main alternative to the left, claiming Zema is diverting attention from the ex-president's son's campaign. Despite the online backlash, Flávio Bolsonaro maintains a good relationship with Zema and considers him a possible vice-presidential option.

item.title: Sob Ricardo Couto, TJRJ ampliou em 79% gastos com penduricalhos
item.description: Under the presidency of Justice Ricardo Couto, currently interim governor of Rio de Janeiro, the Rio de Janeiro State Court of Justice (TJRJ) nearly doubled its spending on 'penduricalhos' in 2025, reaching R$ 878.9 million — a 79% increase from 2024. The surge was driven mainly by the food allowance, which jumped from R$ 330.4 million to R$ 571.2 million, alongside sharp rises in travel allowances, housing aid, and cost-of-living indemnities. Despite being banned by the Supreme Federal Court (STF) in March, benefits such as childcare and housing allowances continue to be paid, according to TJ RJ data disclosed under CNJ norms.

item.title: Enquanto agenda com Lula não sai, Trump já recebeu 4 chefes de Estado
item.description: The meeting between Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Donald Trump at the White House, initially scheduled for March, has not yet taken place due to Trump's focus on the U.S.-Iran conflict. Meanwhile, Trump has already hosted four foreign heads of state in Washington since February: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin, Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae, and King Charles III and Queen Camilla of the United Kingdom. The last contact between Lula and Trump was a phone call on January 26, after which their relationship appears to have cooled, with Lula adopting a more critical stance toward Trump ahead of Brazil's 2026 elections.

item.title: Governo Lula reage à expulsão de delegado da PF e escala tensão diplomática com EUA
item.description: The Lula government invoked the principle of reciprocity following the expulsion of a Brazilian Federal Police delegate by the U.S., which accused him of interfering in an extradition process. The move came after the U.S. revoked the credentials of Marcelo Ivo de Carvalho, a liaison officer with ICE, who had been involved in the detention of former congressman Alexandre Ramagem, a fugitive from Brazilian justice. In response, the Brazilian Federal Police withdrew the credentials of a U.S. immigration agent stationed in Brasília, escalating diplomatic tensions between the two nations.

item.title: Críticas e sátiras não podem ser incluídas no inquérito das fake news
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema, a pre-candidate for President from the Novo Party, released satirical videos using puppets to attack Supreme Court justices such as Gilmar Mendes and Alexandre de Moraes over the Banco Master crisis. While the content straddles the line between humor and offense, there is no legal basis for Mendes to request Zema’s investigation under the fake news inquiry. The article argues that the investigation is being misused to suppress political criticism.

item.title: Acordo UE-Mercosul superará últimas resistências, preveem autoridades
item.description: The EU-Mercosul agreement will enter into provisional force on May 1st, with expectations of full ratification soon despite resistance in France and a legal challenge in the European Parliament. Officials state that concerns have already been addressed in existing treaties and that the provisional status is a legal mechanism previously used by the EU. The Brazilian ambassador to the EU emphasized the deal’s benefits for exports, reducing reliance on China, and securing strategic minerals.

item.title: Prisão pelo ICE tem ponta solta
item.description: The arrest of former deputy Alexandre Ramagem by ICE in the United States contains inconsistencies in the official government version, leaving loose ends that require caution. Lula's campaign should avoid politically exploiting the episode to prevent provoking a new confrontation with Donald Trump, especially as it seeks to regain popularity similar to that achieved through the tariff policy.

item.title: Fim da escala 6x1 passa pela CCJ: quais são os próximos passos para aprovação na Câmara
item.description: The Chamber's Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) approved the end of the 6x1 work schedule, advancing to the formation of a special committee to discuss the bill until the end of May. The proposal aims to reduce the workweek to 40 hours with a 5x2 schedule, including a transition period and potential compensation for businesses.

item.title: Depois de lesão de Estêvão, apostas de que Neymar será convocado para a Copa disparam em site
item.description: The potential serious injury to Estêvão, Chelsea striker and Brazil's top scorer under Ancelotti, has driven up Polymarket bets on Neymar being called up for the 2026 World Cup, with 'yes' reaching 50% on April 22 — its highest level since March 17. Injuries to Éder Militão and Lamine Yamal have added defensive concerns, but betting focus remains on the attack.

item.title: Flávio volta à cartilha de Bolsonaro ao opor agro e indígenas para se aproximar do setor do campo
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) revived his father Jair Bolsonaro's rhetoric by opposing indigenous land demarcation at a major agribusiness event in Sinop (MT), signaling the issue will be central in his 2026 campaign. He pledged not to demarcate any indigenous reserve if his government is in power, aligning with the Bolsonarist strategy of appealing to rural producers through criticism of indigenous and environmental policies. Flávio also presented a package of concessions to the agribusiness sector, including lower-interest credit, reduced bureaucracy, and opposition to the soy moratorium, based on a document submitted by sector entities.

item.title: Insatisfeito, governo quer novo relator da PEC da escala 6 X 1
item.description: The Lula government is dissatisfied with Deputy Paulo Azi (União Brasil-BA), the current rapporteur of the 6X1 workweek PEC, for advocating a gradual reduction to 40 hours weekly with corporate compensation, rather than the immediate 36-hour cut sought by the Planalto. House Speaker Hugo Motta is expected to decide next week on forming the special committee, and while the PT, opposition, and government seek to influence the rapporteur position, Motta favors keeping Azi due to his non-ideological stance to avoid hindering the proposal’s progress.

item.title: "Fizeram conosco, a gente vai fazer com eles", diz Lula sobre EUA
item.description: President Lula praised the Brazilian Federal Police's decision to revoke the diplomatic credentials of a U.S. immigration agent, stating Brazil is applying the principle of reciprocity after the U.S. ordered the departure of Brazilian delegate Marcelo Ivo de Carvalho. Lula said, 'They did it to us, we will do it to them,' expressing hope for renewed dialogue and normalization of bilateral relations. The move followed the U.S. agent’s involvement in the arrest of former deputy Alexandre Ramagem, without prior consultation, violating a bilateral police cooperation agreement.

item.title: Lula dá parabéns a Andrei por retirar credenciais de agente dos EUA
item.description: President Lula congratulated Federal Police Director-General Andrei Rodrigues for revoking the credentials of a U.S. agent in Brazil, in response to the expulsion of Brazilian delegate Marcelo Ivo Carvalho from the United States. The move aims to establish reciprocity after Carvalho’s expulsion, during which he served as a PF liaison officer in Miami and was accused by U.S. authorities of political persecution and attempting to manipulate immigration procedures on behalf of fugitive former deputy Alexandre Ramagem, convicted for attempting a coup. Lula emphasized Brazil’s rejection of foreign interference and expressed hope for renewed dialogue to restore normal bilateral relations.

item.title: Lula ameaça EUA: “O que fizeram conosco, a gente vai fazer com eles”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva publicly endorsed on social media the decision by the Federal Police director-general to suspend the credentials of an American agent operating in Brazil, stating that Brazil will reciprocate if the U.S. continues similar actions against Brazilian officials.

item.title: Lula assina decreto para contratação de 1.000 policiais federais
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed a decree to hire 1,000 federal police officers by the end of 2026, bringing the total new hires since December 2025 to 2,000. He stated that, for the first time, all positions in the Federal Police will be filled, emphasizing the government’s commitment to fighting organized crime. The Justice Minister and the PF Director-General also signed the decree, highlighting its importance in strengthening the institution.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que não demarcará terras indígenas no MT
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for the 2026 presidency, stated he will not demarcate any indigenous lands in Mato Grosso if elected, citing the state's vocation for agricultural production. While rejecting new demarcations, he said he would respect indigenous autonomy in deciding land use, provided it is environmentally responsible. He positioned himself as the 'agribusiness candidate,' emphasizing the need for predictability, credit, and security for the sector.

item.title: Aneel aprova reajustes de 5% a 15% na conta de luz de cidades de nove estados
item.description: Aneel approved tariff adjustments ranging from 5% to 15% for eight energy distributors across nine states, impacting nearly 50 million Brazilians. The average increase projected for 2026 is 8%, above the 4.8% inflation forecast, with CPFL Santa Cruz receiving the highest hike at 15.12%. The Lula government is seeking ways to mitigate the impact, as energy costs remain a central concern for household budgets and inflation.

item.title: Ministro da Saúde diz que Flávio é o “bolsonarinho antivacina”
item.description: Health Minister Alexandre Padilha labeled Flávio Bolsonaro as a 'bolsonarinho antivacina' during a press conference on school immunization, rejecting claims that he is vaccinated and linking his stance to that of his father, Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: STM autoriza coleta de dados sobre trajetória de Bolsonaro no Exército
item.description: The Superior Military Tribunal (STM) authorized the collection of documents regarding Jair Bolsonaro's military trajectory in the Army, including his functional record, disciplinary history, and decorations, to support the judgment that will decide whether he will lose his rank due to a criminal conviction exceeding two years. The measure responds to Bolsonaro's own request and aims to assist in analyzing the loss of his officer status, requested by the Military Public Prosecutor's Office, which also sought the same sanction for other officials convicted in the coup plot. Bolsonaro was sentenced by the STF to 27 years and three months in prison.

item.title: Lula elogia PF por aplicar reciprocidade e retirar credenciais de agente dos EUA
item.description: President Lula praised the Federal Police for revoking the credentials of a U.S. government agent in retaliation for the removal of Brazilian delegate Marcelo Ivo de Carvalho from the United States, citing the principle of reciprocity. He expressed hope that the U.S. would be willing to resume dialogue to normalize bilateral relations. The announcement was made during a ceremony that also authorized the hiring of 1,000 new federal police officers approved in a public competition.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro se solidariza com Zema após ação de Gilmar Mendes
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) expressed solidarity with former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) after Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes filed a crime report against Zema over a satirical video posted during his tenure. Bolsonaro criticized judicial activism, claiming the STF is attempting to influence the 2026 elections, and denounced the inquiry opened against him for alleged slander against Lula, arguing no congressperson has been convicted by the STF for slander since 1988.

item.title: Lula elogia diretor-geral da PF por retirar credenciais de policial dos EUA
item.description: President Lula praised Federal Police Director General Andrei Rodrigues for revoking the credentials of a U.S. immigration agent in retaliation for the U.S. denying credentials to Brazilian Federal Police delegate Marcelo Ivo de Carvalho. Lula framed the move as reciprocity and announced the hiring of 1,000 new federal police officers, stating the government is in a 'war against organized crime'.

item.title: O que EUA fizerem conosco, vamos fazer com eles, diz Lula sobre retirada de credencial a americano
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva praised the director-general of the Federal Police, Andrei Rodrigues, after the blocking of an American immigration agent’s credentials, in response to the Trump administration’s order to remove a Brazilian delegate from the United States. Lula stated that Brazil will reciprocally apply similar measures if the U.S. takes actions against Brazilian officials, reinforcing a stance of equality in diplomatic relations.

item.title: Novo lança pré-candidatura de Kiko Caputo ao governo do DF
item.description: The Novo party officially launched the pre-candidacy of lawyer Kiko Caputo for governor of the Federal District in the 2026 elections during an event at Minas Tênis Clube in Brasília on Wednesday night, the 22nd. The event featured former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema, who is also a Novo pre-candidate for president of Brazil, along with other party pre-candidates for Senate and other offices.

item.title: Ex-presidente do BRB troca advogados e cogita delação
item.description: Former BRB president Paulo Henrique Costa changed his legal team to lawyers Eugênio Aragão and Davi Tangerino on the same day the STF began reviewing his preventive detention. He has been imprisoned since April 16 on suspicion of negotiating R$140 million in bribes to facilitate BRB's acquisition of Banco Master, with investigations indicating luxury real estate was used as payment. A potential plea bargain is being considered.

item.title: Após 4º voto pela condenação de Eduardo Bolsonaro por difamação, Mendonça suspende julgamento
item.description: Minister André Mendonça requested a pause and interrupted the STF trial examining Eduardo Bolsonaro's defamation case against deputy Tabata Amaral. The request came after minister Cristiano Zanin followed rapporteur Alexandre de Moraes, resulting in a 4-0 vote in favor of Bolsonaro's condemnation.

item.title: PDT questiona no Supremo eleição que definiu Douglas Ruas como presidente da Alerj
item.description: The PDT filed an ADPF with the STF challenging the election of Douglas Ruas as president of the Alerj, which was conducted by open vote, arguing that the internal rule change permitting this format lacked proper legislative procedure. The party requests the annulment of the vote and a new secret ballot election, citing risks of undue external interference and violations of constitutional principles such as legislative autonomy, administrative morality, and democratic regime integrity.

item.title: Ministro da Saúde critica Flávio Bolsonaro: ‘Bolsonarinho é antivacina’
item.description: Health Minister Alexandre Padilha criticized Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, calling him 'Bolsonarinho' and accusing him of being antivaccine, noting he did nothing to counter his father Jair Bolsonaro's vaccine denialism during the pandemic. Padilha emphasized that vaccination is a priority for the Lula government, warned about an anti-vaccine presidential candidate, and announced efforts to boost immunization coverage, including an ecumenical event with evangelical leaders.

item.title: Caso Ramagem: Lula diz esperar que EUA voltem a 'conversar' para que a relação volte à 'normalidade'
item.description: President Lula said he hopes the U.S. will resume dialogue to restore normal bilateral relations, following Brazil’s decision to revoke the work credentials of a U.S. official in response to the Trump administration’s action against PF delegate Andrei Rodrigues, who participated in the arrest of Alexandre Ramagem. The Brazilian Foreign Ministry stated the U.S. violated a cooperation agreement by acting without prior notice or dialogue, and confirmed Brazil will apply the principle of reciprocity.

item.title: Lula defenderá fim da jornada 6x1 na primeira propaganda partidária do PT de 2026
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) will advocate for the end of the 6x1 work schedule in the PT’s first 2026 partisan advertisement, set to air nationwide on radio and television starting Thursday, the 23rd. In the spot, Lula will argue the current schedule is unfair to mothers who leave early and return late, proposing a reduction in working hours without salary cuts to strengthen family unity. The ad was previously posted on the PT’s Instagram, gaining 293,000 likes, and comes amid declining presidential approval, which fell to 45.9% according to an Atlas/Bloomberg poll.

item.title: Mendonça pede vista e adia julgamento contra Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: Minister André Mendonça requested a view and halted the STF trial of the defamation case filed by Tabata Amaral against Eduardo Bolsonaro. So far, four justices have voted for conviction, proposing a fine of approximately R$ 85,000. The case, concerning a 2021 post linking the deputy to Jorge Paulo Lemann, is suspended without a set date for resumption.

item.title: A reação de Lula à retirada de credenciais de agente dos EUA após caso Ramagem
item.description: President Lula praised the Federal Police's decision to revoke the credentials of a U.S. agent in retaliation for the U.S. sending back a Brazilian delegate involved in the Alexandre Ramage arrest, stressing reciprocity in international relations. He also announced the hiring of 1,000 new federal police officers to strengthen public security. The Itamaraty criticized the move as violating diplomatic best practices and lacking prior dialogue with the United States.

item.title: Governo Lula gastou R$350 milhões para alugar cruzeiros durante a COP30
item.description: The federal government spent R$350 million on cruise ship rentals to host delegations during COP30, held in Belém in November 2025, according to a document from the Civil House sent to the Chamber of Deputies. The expenditure was justified as necessary to address a shortage of hotel accommodations and local infrastructure to accommodate the large number of participants at the UN climate conference.

item.title: Valdemar encontra Eduardo nos EUA e diz estar confiante na escolha de André do Prado para o Senado
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto said he is confident André do Prado will be the PL's Senate candidate for São Paulo after meeting with Eduardo Bolsonaro in the U.S. Although Eduardo holds the final say, the PL has already unified behind André, who is seen as a loyal ally of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas and key in state legislative coordination. The decision comes amid right-wing divisions over avoiding ideological candidacies that could advantage the left.

item.title: Oposição busca impeachment de Gilmar Mendes e Dino propõe reforma do Judiciário
item.description: The opposition in the Chamber is seeking the impeachment of Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes after he requested the inclusion of former governor Romeu Zema in the fake news investigation. At the same time, Justice Flávio Dino proposed a judicial reform to restore public trust in the justice system.

item.title: Lula elogia retirada de credenciais de agente americano no Brasil: 'O que eles fizeram conosco, a gente vai fazer com eles'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva praised the Federal Police for revoking the diplomatic credentials of a U.S. agent operating in Brazil, calling it a reciprocal measure after the U.S. requested the removal of Brazilian delegate Marcelo Ivo de Carvalho, who participated in the arrest of former deputy Alexandre Ramagem in the United States. Lula stated, 'What they did to us, we will do to them,' and expressed hope for renewed dialogue and normalization of bilateral relations. The move suspends the agent’s access to PF units and shared police databases, in line with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ criticism of the U.S. for failing to follow diplomatic best practices between friendly nations.

item.title: Flávio diz que Zema é vítima de militância do Judiciário e volta a acusar STF de interferência eleitoral
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) claims former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) is 'another victim of judicial militancy' and accuses the STF of interfering in the electoral process to imbalance the race. He reiterates criticism of the Supreme Federal Court, alleging its rulings favor opposing candidates.

item.title: PL deve apoiar PEC 6x1, mas quer novo regime de contratação e compensação
item.description: The PL, Brazil's main opposition party, signaled support for PEC 6x1, which aims to end the 6x1 work schedule — a key banner of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in the 2026 electoral year. However, the party demands a new hiring and compensation regime for affected workers. This move reflects an attempt to balance labor agendas with sectoral demands in a highly polarized electoral context.

item.title: Rede Sustentabilidade endossa candidatura de Marina ao Senado e chama Tarcísio de 'desastroso'
item.description: The São Paulo state executive of the Rede Sustentabilidade party endorsed Marina Silva's pre-candidacy for the Senate and harshly criticized Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, calling his administration 'disastrous'. The endorsement comes amid efforts to build alliances for the 2026 elections, focusing on environmental and sustainability agendas.

item.title: Zema sobre ser vice: 'O que existe são 3 candidaturas e vou levar a minha até o final'
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential pre-candidate for the Novo party, stated he was not officially approached by Flávio Bolsonaro to be his vice-presidential running mate. Despite the lack of an invitation, Zema affirmed he intends to maintain his presidential candidacy through the end of the 2026 elections, noting there are currently three candidacies in play.

item.title: Me comprometo com fim da moratória da Soja, diz Flávio Bolsonaro durante a agro Norte Show
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for President in 2026, defended ending the Soy Moratorium during the Agro Norte Show, stating his commitment to the measure. He argued that the agreement, which prohibits companies from buying soy produced in deforested areas of the Amazon, harms rural producers.

item.title: Flávio diz que espera ser “candidato do agro” como seu pai
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) said he hopes to be the 'agribusiness candidate' in the 2026 elections during the Norte Show in Sinop (MT), emphasizing the legacy of the Bolsonaro government for the sector. He stated that agribusiness grew under deregulated credit and lower interest rates, and that his visit aimed to listen to demands to formulate commitments for a more prosperous and internationally respected agribusiness.
